name: Body-heat health patch
subtitle: a health sensor patch powered by body warmth

effect: some crystals conduct only along their surface, where nothing scatters the current
how: Health patches that track heart rhythm or blood oxygen need recharging every few days, which is when people stop wearing them. The patch turns the small warmth difference between skin and air into current using thin films of bismuth telluride, which is also a topological insulator; shaping it so current runs through its scatter-free surface could raise the output enough to run the sensor nonstop.
obstacle: Whether surface currents really improve heat-to-power conversion at body temperature is still unproven.
why: Body-heat wearables run only tiny loads; the topological boost is only predicted.
real: Topological-insulator surface states have been studied for boosting thermoelectric zT, and wearable Bi2Te3 generators exist, but no wearable that exploits TI surface states was found.
